text:
Artemi Panarin turned 35 on Oct. 30 and is still the player opponents plan around. In his first full season as a King he has 18 points in 15 games (8 goals, 10 assists), eight of them on the power play, while playing nearly 22 minutes a night.

His best night was the four-assist game against the Sharks on Nov. 4, when he and Adrian Kempe combined for eight points. That is the Panarin the Rangers knew for years: the puck goes to him, and the next shot belongs to someone else. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 91st percentile among forwards.

Two things are pulling in opposite directions. He is shooting 17% on 5.5 expected goals, so his own goals should cool. But at five on five the Kings own 61% of expected goals with him on the ice and have scored 5.4 goals fewer than those chances deserve. If that evens out, the assists should come in bunches. Our range has him finishing around 92 points.
headline: Panarin keeps setting the table in Los Angeles
